intervention_reasons: Orchestrator measured the one-iteration wall directly (traced the wedge to the ipark rendezvous cell at (5,1), dumped its memory) and handed over a specific diagnosis. THE DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG ON BOTH HALVES and the builder refuted it by measurement — see notes.

prompts.text: FOC closed loop on one array; measure the loop rate under FULL SATURATION.
Fix the diagnosed stale-arrival-register defect; prove the chain streams; measure the sustained rate.

notes:
=== examples/foc_motor (2026-08-31/09-01, claude-fable-5) — SHIPPED, PARTIAL SCOPE ===

THE NUMBER: 17,861.5 ns per control iteration to the complete duty packet (17,576.9 ns to the first word), duty-word cadence 142.29 ns, 634 instructions/iteration across 45 active cells => 56.0 kHz equivalent loop rate, ABOVE the 10-40 kHz industrial FOC band. simKYT timing model, NOT silicon-certified.

THE SATURATION REQUIREMENT COULD NOT BE MET, AND THAT IS THE RESULT. The chain has NO STEADY STATE: a SECOND iteration emits nothing (post-group Deadlock = a REAL wedge by INV-67, not a healthy hold); queue_words_physical arm-saturated drive of even ONE iteration emits nothing; reversed arm order emits nothing. Cause composes from documented per-block limits: CordicRotateBlock (N=3) and SVPWMBlock (N=2) each carry a measured whole-burst depth of ONE. All three boundaries pinned as guards that FAIL IF THE WALL MOVES, rather than quoting an indefensible rate. Consequences reported rather than papered over: (a) the INV-19 saturated==per-sample gate cannot be satisfied at CHAIN level (saturated drive yields zero output); (b) no closed-loop settle test — the MEASUREMENT half (Clarke + forward Park) does not co-fit with the command half on one array, so a host-plant settle test would have measured a chain that cannot be built. The builder stopped rather than ship a proxy that passes while proving nothing.

SCOPE SHIPPED: the COMMAND half — 2x PI -> CordicRotate(+theta, inverse Park) -> SVPWM -> three duties. 87/120 cells, hand-placed anchors + auto_route_all (route-only; auto_pnr repacks and triggers the INV-70 wedge). Bit-exact on the real placed+routed+built chip against a golden assembled from the blocks' own pinned integer models. A separate gate proves the MEASUREMENT half (Clarke + forward Park, 75 cells) routes and is bit-exact, so the README's claim about the other half is ENFORCED, not asserted.

PIPELINE_LOCK TRADE, measured one stage down where a steady state exists (PI alone, saturated): True = 949.2 ns/sample (1.054 M/s), False = 893.2 ns (1.120 M/s) — ~6% cost, KEPT ON; correctness under saturation is not tradeable. Its single-shot 1,338.5 ns vs 949.2 ns steady state is the fill-vs-steady gap the deep chain never gets to show.

INV-71: a chain of N=2/N=3 LOCK rendezvous blocks is ROUTING-bound, not cell-bound. The full loop is 55 cells of 120 and still does not fit; over ~2600 placements the best whole-chain result left 2 of 13 nets unrouted, ALWAYS an arm. Cost such designs by ARM COUNT (8 here), not cells. THE TRAP THAT COST THE MOST TIME: nets fanned straight from x16_in into arms report DISTINCT entry/data_addrs (the signature suites accept them as distinct arms) but the SAME hop, so all land on one face, the LOCK bars them, and the chain builds, routes and emits ZERO with every run reporting QueueEmpty. The gate now asserts three distinct HOPS.

INCIDENTAL FIX: test_catalog.py::TestDiscovery was ALREADY BROKEN on pristine main — the FOC blocks landed earlier the same day introduced categories 'control' and 'motor_control' that were never registered. I independently CONFIRMED the 2 failures on main before the merge and 1219/1219 after. A same-day registration gap that no block's own suite could see.

ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION: engine/router diff EMPTY; 17/17 FOC gates reproduced; the two known-limit guards read and confirmed to assert the WALL (they demand re-measurement if it moves); test_catalog broken-then-fixed confirmed by running both trees; placekyt 1219 re-run post-merge; dashboard clean; INV-71 already numbered by the builder's landing.

=== STREAMING FIX (2026-09-01, claude-opus-5) — THE CHAIN NOW STREAMS ===

MY HANDED-OVER DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG ON BOTH HALVES, and the builder refuted it by measurement rather than implementing it. I had traced the wedge to the ipark rendezvous cell and dumped stale words, concluding 'arrival registers vx/vy/vt never clear; fix with reset_per_batch'. Two measurements killed it: (1) the wedged dump is only PARTIALLY stale — [6] and [7] held iteration 1's NEW y and theta, so the cell was accepting two of three arms and was BARRED ON ARM X, not occupied; stale state was the SYMPTOM. (2) reset_per_batch could not have worked at all — it is applied by SimServer._apply_batch_reset once per process_batch RPC, and the FOC harness drives inject_data_physical/chip.run directly, so the spec never executes.

REAL ROOT CAUSE: INV-69, in the one block that never received the fix. CordicRotateBlock's serialize-LOCK release was a value-carrying WRITE.CFG whose face came from an authored unlock_face DataWord in the abutting `pre` cell; the build's _apply_rendezvous_input_faces patches face words in the RENDEZVOUS CELL ONLY, so that copy kept the authored WEST while the router landed arm x on NORTH. The decisive read was read_config(rdv): boot 0x7100 -> after-iter0 0x6100 -> unchanged when wedged; LOCK stayed set and LOCK_FACE went north->west and STUCK. INV-69 had EXPLICITLY NAMED CordicRotate as the next shape it would bite; SVPWM was fixed, the parallel-authored CordicRotate never got it. FIX: port SVPWM's shipped construction — a `relock` entry re-pointing LOCK_FACE from its own reconciled face_x, reached by a backward JUMP declared in internal_jumps (NOT internal_connections — a data edge at a real port makes portmap drop the arm) and authored last per INV-53.

SIBLINGS AUDITED, NONE CHANGED: Clarke re-locks inline from its own reconciled face (INV-69's degenerate-safe case); SVPWM already carries the fix; PIController's release is a lock-CLEAR with no face value so INV-69 does not apply, and its iterm/acch/accl reset_per_batch is correct per INV-68.

IT STREAMS. Six consecutive iterations, different inputs, every duty word bit-exact, every run QueueEmpty — verified independently by the orchestrator on the merged tree: 18/18 words exact, sustained interval 17,935.0 ns => 55.76 kHz (builder measured 17,925.1 ns / 55.79 kHz, spread 62.2 ns).

FILL vs STEADY STATE, the honest finding: the sustained interval is within 0.4% of the fill latency, so THE CHAIN RE-ARMS, IT DOES NOT PIPELINE. Each rendezvous bars its arms until the group clears, so exactly one iteration is in flight and the period is WHOLE-CHAIN DEPTH, not the slowest stage. Rate is bought by SHORTENING THE CHAIN, not by deepening it.

STILL OPEN: saturated != per-sample at chain level. queue_words_physical still wedges (EventLimit, zero words) and reversed arm order still wedges — both INV-70 (the three arm corridors share cells), which is routing topology and out of reach of a block change. Distinguishing signature recorded: the INV-69 defect always COMPLETED iteration 0; these wedge on the FIRST.

INV-4 PROOF: re-pointing relock at an unreconciled word is geometry-preserving (still places, routes, builds) and collapses the chain to exactly one packet, failing all three streaming gates. Landed as a permanent on-chip mutation gate.

NEW INV-72: a rendezvous fix is a FAMILY obligation — static check that no face-carrying WRITE.CFG survives in a NEEDS_DISTINCT_INPUT_FACES block; a PARTIALLY-stale rendezvous dump means a barred arm, not an occupied cell; reset_per_batch is a packet-boundary mechanism, so check the delivery path before reaching for it.

BUILDER'S OWN GOTCHA, worth keeping: golden() must be called ONCE over the whole sequence — the PI integrators evolve across samples (INV-68), so per-iteration calls cold-start the accumulator and produce a false 'not exact' reading.

ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION: engine/router diff EMPTY; 220 block+example tests reproduced in-worktree; my own 6-iteration streaming run on the merged tree bit-exact at 55.76 kHz; placekyt 1219 re-run post-merge; INV-72 numbered by the builder at landing.
